text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure, lower the risk of stroke, and protect kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes. While generally well tolerated, it can cause side effects ranging from mild and temporary to serious.
Most mild side effects improve over time as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory symptoms (cold-like symptoms, stuffy nose, or sinus pressure)
Digestive issues (mild nausea, diarrhea, or stomach upset)
Dry cough (much less common with losartan than with ACE inhibitors, though still possible in some people)

text_blocks.snippet: Contact your doctor or seek prompt medical care if you experience:

list.snippet: High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, slow or irregular heartbeat, or numbness/tingling.
Kidney problems: Decreased urination, swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet, or unexplained weight gain.
Severe low blood pressure (hypotension): Fainting, severe dizziness, or extreme lightheadedness.
Liver issues: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark urine.
Angioedema or severe allergic reaction: Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or severe difficulty breathing or swallowing.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about usage precautions through the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or review detailed side effects on GoodRx Losartan Overview.
